## Head minus tail in three dimensions {#iv3-three-dimensions .vector-lesson .component-lesson .position-lesson}

For $A(x,y,z)$ and $B(u,v,w)$,

$$\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{bmatrix}u-x\\v-y\\w-z\end{bmatrix}.$$

The same rule applies: subtract corresponding coordinates, including the third component.

::: {.takeaway}
Head minus tail works in both 2D and 3D.
:::

::: notes
No spatial applet is needed. Identify B as the head and A as the tail, then subtract corresponding coordinates. The position vectors OA=(x,y,z) and OB=(u,v,w) give AB=OB−OA. Reversing the requested direction negates all three components. Proceed to Example 3.11 for an application.
:::
